My first week as a lab tech in Science City, I thought it would be fun to give names to our test subjects. Knowing how things would turn out, most of the names were people with whom I had an axe to grind.
Plenty of teachers and professors.
Ex-lovers. All three of them.
Most were named after childhood bullies. And a few adult ones, for good measure.
Criminals, politicians, landlords...easy targets.

Once the experiments began and the side-effects started kicking in, I realized what a mistake that was. Seeing these creatures as anything more than a statistic really began to take a toll. Makes your work harder, more...emotional.
I've relied on classification numbers ever since.
Limiting your exposure is crucial to survival. Both physically and emotionally.
